function the row names that P2 did not return: IOBoard.md:524 lists 'its balance-lead input network ... not stated (R9)' as an open item of the cell monitor. It is the per-tap resistors and capacitors in front of the ADBMS1818's C pins, so its part is a resistor or capacitor. Research.md (Round 2, Rules of stage 1) says such a function is returned without candidates and left to stage 2; P2 returned no entry for it, and FU-2P1's P1-R9 function list names only 'Cell monitor' and 'cell monitor isolation barrier'.

function the row names that P2 did not return: IOBoard.md:524 names 'protection against a mis-plugged lead' and IOBoard.md:575 puts ESD and overvoltage protection on the balance-lead connector in round 2; Research.md Scope row 2 and the stage 1 rules leave it to stage 2 and require an entry without candidates. P2 returned none. P2's rank 1 reason relies on this function ('stage 2's balance-lead protection for a reversed lead'), and V188 (85 V) and V191 (shifted lead, reversed 67.2 V) are its requirement values.

function the row names that P2 did not return: IOBoard.md:524 names 'the balance-lead connector sizes'; V192 (owner, 2026-09-28) fixes 1 connector of 16 cells, 17 pins, with each pack's leads arriving through an adapter lead. Connectors are selected in stage 2 and are returned without candidates in stage 1. P2 returned no entry.

function the row names that P2 did not return: V193 (owner, 2026-09-28): no jumper or adapter lead sets the cell count and 'the board ties unused inputs itself'. That is a function of the board, in front of the monitor's inputs, not named in the R9 row or IOBoard.md. P2 returned no entry. Its part is not stated: if resistors or diodes it is stage 2; if an active part it is a stage 1 part. P2's rank 1 reason also requires V+ held at 16 V or more for packs under 16 V, which implies a supply referenced to the pack's negative; that supply is in no function list.

followUps.reason: function the row names that P2 did not return: Not named by the R11 row or its IOBoard.md lines, so it is outside the strict definition; reported because P2's rank 1 for 'accelerometer' meets the 'lead length' value (V222) only 'with 100 pF on XOUT and a buffer before the lead', and no entry or part for that buffer is in what I was given. ADXL316's 32 kohm output resistor cannot drive the lead capacitance without the pole moving into the delay-variation node, and the buffer's own delay variation counts inside the 1.244 us share. If P2's full record already names a buffer part, this item closes. Every function that the row and its IOBoard.md lines do name (accelerometer, optical index, magnetic pickup, phase-wire clip, encoder input, encoder decode, rotation from ESC, BENCH rpm source, servo measured position, with 'rotation inputs' as P2's own addition) has a P2 entry.

requirements.name: isolator supply
requirements.required: VREG also supplies the barrier's pack side
requirements.datasheet: VREG is a 5 V input, 4.5 to 5.5 V (Table 3), made by an NPN driven from DRIVE: DRIVE gives 5.7 V and sources 1 mA, the NPN needs a beta over 40, and 'the peak VREG current requirement of the ADBMS1818 approaches 35 mA'. 'If the VREG pin is required to support any additional load, a transistor with an even higher Beta may be required' (p. 71). The device's own VREG draw in 4-wire SPI is at most 16.5 mA (core, measure) plus 8.1 mA (ISOMD = 0, active, RB1 + RB2 = 2 kΩ) (Table 3). DRIVE is 0 V in the sleep state (p. 25), so an isolator on that VREG is unpowered in sleep; see the report

report.value: V289 puts the isolator's pack side on the ADBMS1818's VREG. VREG is made from DRIVE through an NPN, and DRIVE is 0 V in the sleep state (p. 25), so the isolator's pack side is unpowered then. The monitor enters sleep tSLEEP = 1.8 to 2.2 s after the last valid command (Table 4). In 4-wire SPI it wakes only on activity on CSB or SCK: a differential SCK - CSB of at least 200 mV for at least 240 ns (Table 7, p. 56). An isolator output with no supply cannot drive that, so the coprocessor cannot wake a sleeping monitor through any candidate. The data sheet allows 'VREG can be powered by an external supply' (p. 25). That would keep the isolator powered, but its quiescent current would then flow from the pack: 2.0 to 5.2 mA for ISO7741, 11 to 19.5 µA for ISO7041 (DC). Keeping the monitor awake with a command every 1.8 s or less needs it awake first. The data sheet text read does not state its state after V+ is applied. The owner decides how VREG is supplied

found_values.value: 1.244 us of delay variation at 1,092 Hz (65,535 rpm) for the optical index: the sensor, its front end and the index comparator together. Found from V225 and V290: 1 degree of the 915.5 us period at 65,535 rpm is 2.543 us for the whole chain (V225); R10's own share is 52 ns, its 30 ps aperture jitter and the chip-select trigger jitter inside (V290, V291); the rest is split equally between the accelerometer and the optical index, (2.543 - 0.052) / 2 = 1.246 us, which V290 writes as 1.244 us. The split leaves no separate share for the index comparator, so its delay counts inside the 1.244 us. At 10,000 rpm the same split gives (16.67 - 0.342) / 2 = 8.16 us

report.value: Two PIO state machines in PIO0 of the measurement coprocessor (encoder A, B and I on GPIO 20, 21, 22), one per channel, run one copy of quad_edge.pio (19 instruction words); no external decoder, no DMA channel, no PWM slice for A and B. Each edge takes at most 6 clk_sys cycles (40 ns at 150 MHz) against 100 ns between one channel's edges at 5 MHz (80 ns at 40/60 duty), so 2 state machines decode 20 Mcounts/s; 1 MHz single-ended is 4 Mcounts/s. A cycle model with the 2-flipflop input synchroniser decodes 40,000 counts at 5 MHz without error at A-to-B spacing 30 and 70 ns, duty 40 to 60 %, 3 ns jitter and 200 reversals, and 1 MHz with 50 reversals; it decodes down to 14 ns of A-to-B spacing and fails at 13 ns. The receiver's opposite-edge delay difference across two channels of one AM26LV32EIDR is at most 26 - 8 = 18 ns (tPLH and tPHL 8 to 26 ns; the 9 ns tsk(pp) is a device-to-device figure and does not apply), which leaves 32 ns; the model decodes 32 ns at 40, 50 and 60 % duty with 3 ns jitter and 100 reversals. The counts sit in the RX FIFO in put mode (FJOIN_RX_PUT), read at any time; net = Y(A) - X(A) + X(B) - Y(B) modulo 2^32; a read while the shaft turns can mix counts a few edges apart, and the error does not accumulate. The index I is captured on the same chip's clock, by a GPIO edge interrupt on the 1 us system timer or by PIO. pico-examples' one-state-machine quadrature_encoder reads only sysclk / 10 = 15 Msteps/s. No quadrature decoder from an allowlisted maker is in the jlcparts copy. Derived from the datasheet's instruction timing and the model; not run on hardware; the program is not in the tree

report.figure: barrier unpowered in monitor sleep (P2's report, re-read)
report.value: Confirmed. In the sleep state the DRIVE pin is 0 V (p. 25); tSLEEP is 1.8 / 2.0 / 2.2 s after the last valid command (Table 4); in SPI mode activity on CSB or SCK wakes the port (p. 56). VREG is made from DRIVE through an NPN, so an isolator pack side on VREG is unpowered in sleep and cannot pass the wake-up. 'VREG can be powered by an external supply' (p. 25), then 3.1 µA flows in sleep (Table 3). Not found in the text read: the monitor's state when V+ is first applied. The serial interface goes idle after tIDLE of 4.3 / 5.5 / 6.7 ms with no activity. This stays open for the owner and P5
report.source: ADBMS1818 Rev. B pp. 25, 26, 56, Tables 3 and 4, SHA-256 36b07646...c7cbfbfb, read 2026-10-02T00:55:41Z

report.value: Core 16.5 mA + isoSPI 8.1 mA = 24.6 mA, plus the isolator's ICC2 bound at 5 V: ISO7741DWR and ISO7741DBQR 6.4 mA = 31.0; ISO6741DWR 6.5 = 31.1; ISO7341CDWR 6.5 = 31.1; ISO7841DWWR 6.1 = 30.7; ISO7141CCDBQR 9.6 = 34.2; ADUM1411BRWZ-RL 2.4 = 27.0; ADUM1401BRWZ-RL 1.8 = 26.4; ADUM7441CRQZ-RL7 4.6 = 29.2 at 1 Mbps and 35.6 at its 25 Mbps column; ISO7041DBQR 0.211 = 24.8 at 1 Mbps with no load. The 35 mA is the data sheet's peak with simultaneous isoSPI and conversions, not a limit: 'a transistor with an even higher Beta may be required' for more (p. 71). TI's tables give 1 and 10 Mbps at VCC1 = VCC2 only, so 10 Mbps bounds the 2 Mbps SPI clock; ADuM1411, ADuM1401 and ADuM7441 tabulate mixed 3.3 V/5 V supplies
report.source: ADBMS1818 Rev. B Table 3 and p. 71; isolator data sheets as listed in each record, read 2026-10-02T00:55:37Z to 01:05:52Z

report.figure: SDO return path and the 50 ns footnote
report.value: t8 (SCK falling to SDO valid) is 60 ns at most and 'does not include rise or fall time of SDO'; the rise depends on the 5 kΩ pull-up and the load capacitance, and the data sheet asks that it meet the microcontroller's setup time (Table 10 note). Round trips before that rise, at 1 MHz (500 ns half period): ISO7741 97 ns, ISO6741 96, ISO7841DWWR 92, ISO7141CC 150, ADuM1401B 160, ADuM1411B 180, ADuM7441C 180, ISO7341C 192, ISO7041 410. The load capacitance and the RP2354B's setup are not read. Table 9's tCLK, t6 and t7 'include allowances for 50 ns of delay in each direction' of cable; whether an isolator's delay above 50 ns (ISO7041 175 ns, ISO7341C 66 ns, ADuM1411B 60 ns, ADuM7441C 60 ns) derates them in 4-wire SPI is not stated
report.source: ADBMS1818 Rev. B Tables 9 and 10 with notes, p. 9-10, read 2026-10-02T00:55:41Z; isolator timing tables as listed in each record

P2's three parts clamp to both rails (TLV3201 -0.5 V to VCC + 0.5 V, TLV3501 and TLV3601 -0.3 V to VCC + 0.3 V). With the rail down, a coasting motor's divided phase signal flows into the rail through the divider on TLV3201, TLV3501, TLV3601 and TLV1811, and into nothing on TLV7011 and TLV7031 up to 6 V and 7 V. Stage 2's divider sets the current in each case

report.value: P3's missed function holds. P2's rank 1 meets the lead-length value (V222: 2 m, its capacitance outside the delay-variation node) only with a buffer between XOUT and the lead, and no function or part selects that buffer. data.ruling: The datasheet verifier's refutation stands on "converter delay variation". V290 (Research.md:987, owner, 2026-10-01) sets a delay-variation share for this function's converter: 52 ns at 65,535 rpm and 342 ns at 10,000 rpm. That share holds the aperture jitter and the trigger's jitter. V291 (Research.md:988) puts the trigger and timer jitter inside the same 52 ns. The Follow-ups row (Research.md:587) applies this budget to "Converter for the accelerometer". In the reference option, the converter is the RP2354B's own ADC. Its data sheet gives no aperture jitter, no aperture delay and no start-to-sample latency, so the 52 ns cannot be confirmed from it. A value that is not read does not pass the gate. The re-rank marked the check "pass: true" while its own text reads "Not confirmed against 52 ns". That marking is wrong. The "trigger on the coprocessor timebase" check also fails, which supports the ruling. The ADC has no external trigger input and no chip-select edge. A conversion starts in only two ways: a register write to CS.START_ONCE, or the ADC's own pacing timer, which runs on clk_adc. The data sheet states no relation between a sample instant and the clk_sys timebase on which the index pulse is sampled. Timestamping each sample by its index is an inference, not a data sheet statement. The LM4040 passes every check of its own: ADC_AVDD 2.978 to 3.032 V; 5.51 mA left for the loads from 30 Ohm on the 3.3 V rail; stock 2,969 at JLCPCB and 26,680 at Digi-Key; status ACTIVE. The stock verifier confirmed these and the datasheet verifier did not dispute them. The refutation is about the option's converter against this function's requirement, so scope is function. Every reference part in this option fails the same way. The ruling does not touch Q4's decision for the external ADC, ADCS7476AIMFX/NOPB (Research.md:1002, 2026-09-29).
data.evidence:
RP2350 data sheet, build-date 2025-07-29 (served as RP-008373-DS-2, 7,968,417 bytes), re-read by this adjudicator:
- 12.4.3: "Capturing a sample takes 96 clock cycles (96 x 1/48 MHz) = 2 us per sample (500 kS/s)". The section names no aperture jitter, no aperture delay and no start latency.
- 12.4.3.1: "Write a 1 to CS.START_ONCE to immediately start a new conversion". This register write is the only one-shot start.
- 12.4.3.2: with CS.START_MANY, "Set DIV.INT to a positive value n to trigger the ADC once per n + 1 cycles". This pacing counts clk_adc cycles. A non-zero DIV.FRAC alternates the interval between two values.
- Table 1438 (ADC characteristics) lists only these rows: VPIN_ADC 0 to ADC_AVDD; ENOB 9 min, 9.5 typ; 12 resolved bits; RIN_ADC 100 kOhm min. It has no timing row.
- 12.4.5: "INL and DNL: Details to follow."
- A text search of the whole data sheet for "aperture", "external trigger" and "trigger input" finds no ADC entry. The only hits are flash-window aperture sizes and the debug CTI triggers.

Requirement:
- V290 (Research.md:987): 52 ns at 65,535 rpm and 342 ns at 10,000 rpm. The share holds the aperture jitter and the trigger's jitter. "PIO or a timer of the measurement coprocessor drives the trigger".
- V291 (Research.md:988): "The trigger and timer jitter sits inside V290's 52 ns".
- IOBoard.md "Vibration delay": "a constant delay cancels; its variation counts".
- IOBoard.md "Timebase": the accelerometer and the index pulse are sampled on the measurement coprocessor's timebase.

Re-rank of FU-2C (scratch/FU-2C/rerank-R10/final.json), rank 7: "converter delay variation" is marked "pass": true, and its text reads "Not confirmed against 52 ns: the data sheet does not state it". Sensing.md:110 records for the reference option: "Triggering on the index pulse's timebase is not confirmed in the returns".

The stock and lifecycle checks pass and are not part of the refutation:
- stock: JLCPCB C544506 stockCount 2,969, canPresaleNumber 2,956; Digi-Key 26,680.
- status: TI ACTIVE.

data.ruling: The refutation stands on both points, and both are errors in the reported figure. (1) The claim says the A version has a SINAD of 71.5 dB typ. In Rev. F Table 1 that value is in the B version column only. The A version states 69 dB min over TMIN to TMAX and 70 dB min at 25 degC, and gives no typical SINAD. (2) The rms is wrong in its arithmetic: 28.945 mg / sqrt(12) = 8.356 mg, so 8.36 mg, not 8.34 mg. The core figure holds: ENOB = (69 - 1.76) / 6.02 = 11.17 bits minimum, and the step is 28.9 mg at 15 mV/V/g with a ratiometric full scale of 66.7 g. The 23-sample count also holds: ceil((8.356 / 1.75)^2) = 23. Corrected figure: 11.17 bits minimum from SINAD 69 dB min (A version, -40 to 85 degC, fIN 100 kHz), 70 dB min at 25 degC, no typical given for the A version; 28.9 mg step, 8.36 mg rms, 23 samples to reach 1.75 mg. I did not re-derive the 0.046 mg after 5 s, because it is not part of the refutation. 8.356 mg / sqrt(13,108 x 5) gives 0.033 mg, so the 0.046 mg assumes a per-channel rate the claim does not state. The scope is function: the error is in this function's reported figure, not in the part's lifecycle, maker or identity.
data.evidence: AD7476/AD7477/AD7478 Rev. F, Table 1, page 3, dynamic performance at fIN = 100 kHz. I read the page as rendered (pdftoppm, 110 dpi) and as pdftotext -layout. SINAD rows: A version 69 dB min and 70 dB min at TA = 25 degC. B version 70 dB min and 71.5 dB typ. S version 69 dB min and 70 dB min. The 71.5 sits under the B Version column header, and the A column is blank on the dB typ row. Footnote: temperature range for the A and B versions is -40 to +85 degC. Arithmetic (python3): ENOB = 11.1694 bits; step = (1/0.015 g) / 2^11.1694 = 28.945 mg; rms = 28.945 / 3.4641 = 8.3557 mg; ceil((8.3557 / 1.75)^2) = 23.

data.ruling: The refutation stands. The claim was 'the count comes from the setting (SET_PACK_CELLS)', and no line at 145e028 supports it. SET_PACK_CELLS is defined only in the settings table: settings.c:39-41, 'pack_cells', 'Series count in the pack', 1 to 14, default 6. Apart from that table and settings.h:41, it appears only in test_settings.c and in render_screen.c:333, where the setup-dirty screenshot sets it to 4. No firmware or UI code reads SET_PACK_CELLS into battery_state_t. The only settings_get_int calls in firmware/panel/main/main.c read SET_OUT_RAMP, SET_MOTOR_POLES and SET_OUT_MIN_US/MAX_US. battery_screen.c never reads a setting. battery_screen_set() at battery_screen.c:70-81 copies the whole state struct, cells included, as the caller passes it (s.b = *b). The header documents that struct as 'What the balance lead says' (battery_screen.h:27), so if anything the cell count is tied to the lead, not to the setting. The only callers are the host tests (test_battery.c:59, render_screen.c:324), which set b.cells = 6 directly (render_screen.c:311), as IOBoard.md:433 also says. The presence half of the claim (valid, NO PACK, 'nothing on the lead') matches battery_screen.h:19/27 and battery_screen.c:233. The count half has no source, and the question V195 itself says 'No line states where the count comes from.' The figure as claimed is not found. The finding is about this function's requirement value, not about the part.

Every list value is equal or stronger (1,092 Hz over 167 Hz; 2 axes over one). None omitted.

figures.figure: function requirements: magnetic pickup
figures.evidence: V217 (Hall latch, digital, 3.3 V, open-drain, GPIO 27), V218 (one pulse a turn, 20 kHz bandwidth), V212, V213, V221, V231 and IOBoard.md 'Magnetic pickup: an rpm input' are all in the list; sensitivity is 'no limit' as V217 and V218 give no magnet or gap.

figures.figure: function requirements: phase-wire clip
figures.evidence: V212/V293 (22,937 Hz, rpm = f x 60 / (MOTOR_POLES / 2)), V214 (120 V over IOBoard.md's 67.2 V), V215 (galvanic), V216 (none), V229 (8 to 288 kHz), V213 (not below 500 rpm), V292/V290 (comparator inside 1.244 us where shared), V7 (0 to 50 degC), 3.3 V +/-3 %, Pins.md GPIO 25 are all named; none weaker.

figures.figure: function requirements: encoder input
figures.evidence: F4 (both forms, jumper), V227 (5 MHz and 1 MHz per channel), V228 (12 V), IOBoard.md:483-484 and Pins.md (A, B, I on GPIO 20 to 22, PIO0), 3.3 V rail, V7 (0 to 50 degC) and the powered-off rule are in the list.

figures.figure: function requirements: encoder decode
figures.evidence: IOBoard.md:485 (up to 5 MHz; PIO, DMA, PWM or external decoder reported for P5), V227 (20 and 4 Mcounts/s), F4, Pins.md (index on GPIO 22, PIO0) and rule 2 for an external decoder are in the list.

figures.figure: function requirements: rotation from ESC
figures.evidence: IOBoard.md:479 gives source (period divided by MOTOR_POLES / 2, even 2 to 42, 0 gives none), 200 ms staleness and the DShot stop at disarm (:528); V293 refers to this conversion; no Raised-by-P1 row names the function. All are in the list.

figures.figure: function requirements: rotation inputs
figures.evidence: V212 (65,535 rpm, 1,092 / 22,937 Hz), V213 (10 rpm, clip not below 500 rpm), V211 (own front end and GPIO), IOBoard.md:79, :112, :526-528 and Pins.md are in the list. The 'edge timing' line says every input is timed on the measurement clock, which holds for the five inputs of IOBoard.md:112; the ESC telemetry period is timed on the main.

figures.figure: function requirements: BENCH rpm source
figures.evidence: V211 (one input by a panel setting, register, no selector part) and IOBoard.md:468, :470 (1 rpm a count, 65,535, one valid bit; link_pages.h:233, :250; bench_state.c:21-28) are in the list.
